scenario.title: Compound filters, replacements, removals, prediction, and route change
scenario.focus: Filter stacking and replacement, current-option reasoning, prediction-to-search sequencing, and distinguishing a departure-location change from an airport filter.

turns.user: Find one-way flights from New York to Los Angeles on October 20, 2026 for one adult in economy.
turns.expectedIntent: Start a new exact-date one-way flight search.
turns.why: The route, exact date, passengers, trip type, and cabin are complete, so a new search is required without price prediction.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create a new search key, store three current options, and start with no active filters.
turns.validates: Manager delegates a complete flight request once and Flight does not over-trigger prediction for an exact date.

turns.user: Show only nonstop morning departures under $220 with carry-on baggage.
turns.expectedIntent: Apply four constraints to the current result set in one mutation.
turns.why: Stops, departure time, maximum price, and baggage are supported filters and do not change the search inputs.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the search key and activate stops, departureTime, price, and baggage filters.
turns.validates: One compound apply_filter call, no unnecessary re-search, and complete filter stacking.

turns.user: Make it evening instead, drop the price cap, and remove the carry-on requirement.
turns.expectedIntent: Replace one active filter and remove two others while preserving nonstop.
turns.why: This is an in-place filter update: evening replaces morning, while price and baggage are removed.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the search key with only stops and evening departure active.
turns.validates: Indirect replacement wording and multi-filter removal without losing unrelated state.

turns.user: Remove the nonstop filter, show only Air China, and keep total trip duration under four hours.
turns.expectedIntent: Remove stops and add airline plus total-duration constraints.
turns.why: All requested changes operate on the existing cards; evening departure remains unchanged because it was not removed.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the search key with evening departure, Air China, and maximum total duration active.
turns.validates: Targeted removal, named-airline resolution, duration filtering, and preservation of an unmentioned active filter.

turns.user: Which current option is cheapest, and why?
turns.expectedIntent: Reason over current generated options without changing visibility or search state.
turns.why: A current-option ranking requires fresh contract evidence, not a new search or another filter.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the search key and all active filters unchanged.
turns.validates: Fresh contract retrieval, context reuse, and no state mutation for option reasoning.

turns.user: Check for better travel dates between October 21 and October 28, then show flights on the strongest date with Air China still applied.
turns.expectedIntent: Evaluate a flexible date window, search the strongest or bounded fallback date, then reapply the explicitly retained airline.
turns.why: The flexible bracket requires prediction before the requested search; the new search clears old filters, so only the explicitly retained Air China filter is reapplied.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create a new search key on an in-window date and leave only the Air China filter active.
turns.validates: Prediction-to-search-to-filter ordering, bounded failure fallback, and selective filter carry-forward.

turns.user: Start the trip in Newark instead of New York, using the same date, passengers, and cabin. Keep Air China and remove every other filter.
turns.expectedIntent: Change the departure endpoint, run a new search, and reapply only the requested airline filter.
turns.why: Starting in Newark changes the search route; it is not merely a departure-airport filter on the old New York search.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create a new search key for Newark to Los Angeles and keep only Air China active.
turns.validates: Filter-looking route changes, reuse of prior date/passengers/cabin, and removal of stale filters after re-search.
